dimensions.description: Who or what is affected, and how the failures are spread.
What the sign-in client reports to the user.
What the identity service logs show, or do not show.
The state of the device, its registration and its client.
Changes to policy or network made before the problem.
What the provider status or incident feed says.
Results of name-resolution, proxy and federation checks.
What a fix or a clean-up step did to the problem.
What an engineer did, asked for or arranged.

signals.label: Conditional Access configuration has not changed recently
signals.description: The customer or a config review shows no recent policy change.

signals.label: Excluding users from the MFA policy did not help
signals.description: After users were excluded from the MFA / Conditional Access policy, failures continued.

signals.label: Clearing the client cache or reinstalling did not help
signals.description: Cache clearing, a clean profile, or a reinstall left the failures unchanged.

signals.label: Clearing the client cache fixed the device
signals.description: The device signs in successfully after clearing cache or reinstalling.

signals.label: Failures stopped after the DNS resolver fix
signals.description: After the failing resolver was removed or the DNS policy corrected, failures stopped.

signals.label: Client reports a name-resolution failure
signals.description: The Teams client error tag caa82ee7 (a WinINET "name not resolved" style code) or an ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED / NXDOMAIN message appears.

signals.label: Client reports a connection timeout
signals.description: The Teams client error tag caa82ee2 or an ERR_TIMED_OUT style message appears.

signals.label: Federation server errors, certificate or clock problems
signals.description: AD FS or STS logs show certificate, clock-skew or node errors.

signals.label: Failures are intermittent
signals.description: A retry sometimes succeeds; the failure is not deterministic.

signals.label: MFA / Conditional Access events exist in sign-in logs
signals.description: Sign-in log rows with AADSTS50076, 50074 or Conditional Access failure results are present.

signals.label: Multiple users affected at once
signals.description: More than a handful of users report the same problem in the same period.

signals.label: No server-side sign-in records for the failing attempts
signals.description: Correlating failing attempts (user + UTC time) with Entra sign-in logs finds no matching failure records: the requests never reached the identity service.

signals.label: Policy-related log events do not coincide with the failures
signals.description: Query output was annotated as having zero rows inside the reported failure window, so the policy-related events it found are unrelated background.

signals.label: Failures stopped after the proxy fix
signals.description: After the failing proxy node was removed from rotation or inspection was bypassed, failures stopped.

signals.label: One proxy node times out while others respond
signals.description: A per-node test shows at least one proxy node timing out or failing for sign-in hosts.

signals.label: All proxy nodes respond consistently
signals.description: A per-node test shows every proxy node responding normally.

signals.label: Primary refresh token is healthy on sampled devices
signals.description: dsregcmd output shows AzureAdPrt: YES.

signals.label: Primary refresh token is missing on sampled devices
signals.description: dsregcmd output shows AzureAdPrt: NO.

signals.label: Customer reports a recent Conditional Access change
signals.description: A Conditional Access or MFA policy was changed shortly before onset.

signals.label: A DNS, proxy or filtering change was deployed shortly before onset
signals.description: A network-side policy change (DNS filtering, proxy/TLS inspection, firewall) preceded the failures.

signals.label: One DNS resolver fails or blocks sign-in hosts while others answer
signals.description: A per-resolver name-resolution test shows at least one resolver failing for sign-in or CDN hosts.

signals.label: All DNS resolvers answer sign-in hosts consistently
signals.description: A per-resolver test shows every resolver answering normally.

signals.label: Revoking user sessions did not change the failure rate
signals.description: After sessions were revoked and users signed in again, failures continued unchanged.

signals.label: Failing attempts have matching server-side failure records
signals.description: Correlation finds failed sign-in records at the reported times.

signals.label: No active Microsoft service incident
signals.description: Service health and the Message center show no relevant incident.

signals.label: An active Microsoft service incident matches the symptoms
signals.description: Service health lists an active incident affecting sign-in or Teams.

signals.label: Only one user or device is affected
signals.description: The report is confined to a single user or a single device.

signals.label: Failures concentrate at specific sites or networks
signals.description: Some sites or networks are affected much more than others.

signals.label: Token expiry or session revocation errors in logs
signals.description: Sign-in logs show AADSTS70043, 700082, 50173, 50132 or 50133.

signals.label: The browser version of Teams also fails
signals.description: Teams on the web fails too, so the desktop client is not the sole factor.

actions.label: Bypass TLS inspection for Microsoft 365 endpoints (permanent fix)
actions.description: Exempt Microsoft 365 endpoints from TLS inspection per Microsoft published endpoint guidance, under change control.

actions.label: Review federation server health, certificates and clocks
actions.description: Check AD FS / STS node health, token-signing certificate validity and clock synchronisation.

actions.label: Check Microsoft 365 service health
actions.description: Review Service health and the Message center for active incidents affecting Teams or Microsoft Entra ID.

actions.label: Clear the Teams client cache on a device
actions.description: Ask the customer to clear the Teams cache on an affected device and retry.

actions.label: Send the customer a status update with next steps and timing
actions.description: Tell the customer what was found, what happens next and when they will hear back.

actions.label: Check device registration and PRT health (dsregcmd)
actions.description: Run dsregcmd /status on sampled affected devices and inspect AzureAdPrt and join state.

actions.label: Compare name resolution across each DNS resolver
actions.description: Run Resolve-DnsName for the sign-in and CDN hosts against every DNS resolver used by the affected site and compare the answers.

actions.label: Escalate to the identity backend team
actions.description: Escalate with the evidence collected so far and request backend traces.

actions.label: Temporarily exclude users from the MFA policy
actions.description: Exclude affected users from the MFA Conditional Access policy as a test.

actions.label: Compare sign-in connectivity through each proxy node
actions.description: Test the sign-in endpoints through every proxy or TLS-inspection node from an affected site and compare timings.

actions.label: Reinstall Teams on affected devices
actions.description: Ask the customer to uninstall and reinstall the Teams client.

actions.label: Take the failing proxy node out of rotation (workaround)
actions.description: Temporarily remove the failing proxy node from the PAC file or load balancer.

actions.label: Remove the failing DNS resolver from the affected scopes (workaround)
actions.description: Temporarily remove the failing resolver from DHCP scopes so clients use healthy resolvers.

actions.label: Request HAR / Fiddler traces from end users
actions.description: Ask users to capture a network trace while a sign-in fails, then analyse the large capture.

actions.label: Ask for minimal scoping data
actions.description: Ask the customer for the exact client error text or code, three failing sample users with UTC failure times, and which sites or networks are affected versus unaffected.

actions.label: Ask about recent identity, network or policy changes
actions.description: Ask the customer which identity, network, DNS, proxy or policy changes were made in the 48 hours before onset.

actions.label: Correct the DNS filtering policy (permanent fix)
actions.description: Roll back the faulty DNS filtering rule and add an exception for published Microsoft 365 endpoints, under change control.

actions.label: Review Conditional Access configuration and recent changes
actions.description: Review policy assignments, sign-in frequency settings and the audit log for recent Conditional Access changes.

actions.label: Revoke refresh tokens and sessions for affected users
actions.description: Revoke sign-in sessions so every affected user must authenticate again.

actions.label: Correlate failing attempts with Entra sign-in logs
actions.description: Look up each failing attempt (user + UTC time) in SigninLogs and AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs. No matching failure record means the attempt never reached the identity service.

actions.label: Validate the fix with a before/after comparison
actions.description: Compare failure rates over a monitoring window, re-run the discriminating test, and get customer confirmation.

requirements.label: Scope of impact (who, how many, where)
requirements.description: How many users are affected and whether it is one user, one site, or many.

requirements.label: Business impact confirmed
requirements.description: What the failure prevents the customer from doing and how urgent it is.

requirements.label: Recent environment changes
requirements.description: Network, identity or policy changes shortly before onset.

requirements.label: Client-side diagnostics from a failing attempt
requirements.description: Client logs, network trace or device registration output from a failing attempt.

requirements.label: Customer confirms users can sign in
requirements.description: The customer confirms the problem is resolved for affected users.

requirements.label: Exact client error code or text
requirements.description: The error tag or message shown on a failing client.

requirements.label: Exact failure timestamps (UTC)
requirements.description: UTC times of specific failed attempts, precise enough to correlate with logs.

requirements.label: Fix validated with a before/after comparison
requirements.description: Evidence that failures stopped after the change, over a monitoring window.

requirements.label: Network path check (DNS or proxy) from an affected site
requirements.description: A per-resolver or per-proxy-node test run from an affected site.

requirements.label: Sample affected users
requirements.description: At least one affected user identifier for log lookups.

requirements.label: Server-side sign-in log correlation
requirements.description: Whether failing attempts appear in the identity service logs.

requirements.label: Affected versus unaffected sites or networks
requirements.description: Which locations, networks or device groups are affected and which are not.

requirements.label: Workaround and permanent fix documented separately
requirements.description: The resolution distinguishes the temporary workaround from the permanent fix.

hypotheses.name: Corrupted Teams client cache or WAM broker state
hypotheses.description: Local Teams cache or Web Account Manager state on affected devices is corrupted, so sign-in fails on those devices regardless of network or policy.

hypotheses.name: Conditional Access or MFA policy enforcement
hypotheses.description: A Conditional Access or MFA policy change forces interactive sign-in or blocks attempts, producing server-side sign-in failures that align in time with the reported failures.

hypotheses.name: Device registration or primary refresh token health
hypotheses.description: Affected devices have unhealthy registration or no primary refresh token, so silent sign-in fails and the user is prompted or blocked.

hypotheses.name: DNS resolution failure for sign-in endpoints
hypotheses.description: One or more DNS resolvers used by the affected network intermittently fail to resolve Microsoft sign-in or CDN hosts, so the sign-in page never finishes loading before authentication starts.

hypotheses.name: Federation or identity-provider node issue
hypotheses.description: A federation server (STS) node has an expired certificate, clock skew, or a fault, causing sign-in failures for the share of users routed to it.

hypotheses.name: Other or not yet characterised
hypotheses.description: Probability mass the pack cannot attribute to a named hypothesis. It shrinks as evidence accumulates.

hypotheses.name: Egress proxy or TLS-inspection node failure
hypotheses.description: A web proxy or TLS-inspection node in a proxy pool times out or drops connections to sign-in endpoints, so some attempts fail depending on which node serves the request.

hypotheses.name: Microsoft-side service incident
hypotheses.description: A service incident or regional degradation affects sign-in for many tenants at once.

hypotheses.name: Token or session lifetime problem
hypotheses.description: Refresh tokens or sessions expire, are revoked, or hit sign-in frequency limits, forcing repeated authentication that sometimes fails.
